Article Title: On National Space Day, PM Modi hails Gen Z for building new tech; Isro chief says plan to launch 8 vehicle, 12 satellite missions
Article Text:
PM Modi interacting with CEOs of 20 space startups in New Delhi on Friday

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: On the 3rd National Space Day, PM Narendra Modi on Sunday hailed India's global rise in the space sector and praised Gen Z for building new technologies, saying this rise has made India a “magnet” for global investors.Sharing a video of his speeches, PM Modi said, “I said in Ayodhya that this is the beginning of a new cycle of change. In this new cycle, India is steadily expanding its space presence in the global order, and this is clearly reflected in our space programme. Together, we have resolved to make India a developed nation by 2047, and the space sector plays a vital role in achieving this goal.”Praising the youth of the nation, the PM said, “Today, these Gen Z engineers, designers, coders and scientists are building new technologies. Be it propulsion systems, composite materials, rocket stages or satellite platforms, India's youth is working in areas that were not even imagined some time ago.” He also hailed the private space sector saying, “India's private space talent is making its own identity in the world. ”Just two days ago, the PM interacted with CEOs and founders of 20 space startups on Friday and highlighted India's cost-competitiveness in launching space ventures.He emphasised that the country's vast talent pool and high risk-taking capacity would allow India to rapidly establish a dominant position in the global space sector, according to the transcript of the interaction, which was released on Sunday. One of the CEOs told the PM that after India opened the space industry for private players, a very positive trend was observed and many Indian citizens living in the US and Europe now want to return and work in the country. In response, Modi said: “We need to connect with many people â€“ people who went abroad are now returning. I believe we should create an aura where people worldwide feel that if they want to make a career, they should go to India." He said such people from across the globe should feel that they should connect with a startup in India, connect with a space agency in India.Praising Isro, he said, “Seeing the success of Isro, many children think that when they grow up, they too will become scientists.”Speaking at the 3rd National Space Day celebrations in Ahmedabad, Isro chairman V Narayanan said India’s space programme is heading into a crucial phase, with the agency planning eight launch vehicle missions and 12 satellite missions during the current financial year. Among the most closely watched missions is the first uncrewed flight under the Gaganyaan programme, which Isro expects to undertake within the next four months, he said. Narayanan said the Gaganyaan programme had completed about 8,000 tests and was now approaching its final stage. “We are in the final leg,” he said.Space minister Jitendra Singh said on X, “On National Space Day, we remember the historic success of Chandrayaan-3, a moment that placed India among the world’s leading spacefaring nations. Remarkable achievement of our scientists, backed by the progressive vision of PM.PM Shri Narendra Modi continues to inspire generations. Celebrating our scientists, innovators and the unstoppable spirit of ViksitBharat. ”With the historic milestone of 100 launches and 548 satellites placed in orbit, including around 460 in the last decade alone, India’s space sector is reaching new horizons, petroleum and natural gas minister Hardeep Singh Puri said on Sunday.
Article Summary: Pm narendra modi on sunday hailed india's global rise in the space sector. He praised gen z for building new technologies, saying this rise has made india a “magnet” for global investors. Pm interacted with ceos and founders of 20 space startups on friday.

Article Title: India’s satellite launch cost 4x US, says Cambridge study; space dept source contradicts report
Article Text:
India’s space price tag comes under scrutiny as Cambridge research flags high launch costs, while the government says key subsidies and savings were overlooked

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A 2026 University of Cambridge study has found that India’s per-kilogram launch costs are four times higher than America’s and, in fact, the costliest in the world. However, a highly-placed source in the Department of Space told TOI that the study has not factored in India’s subsidies, saving cost in transport and logistic costs and space manoeuvre costs.A peer-reviewed paper published in the respected Elsevier journal Economics Letters by economists Alessio Terzi of the University of Cambridge and Francesco Nicoli of Politecnico di Torino, Turin, points at a novel database covering more than 6,740 rocket launches between 1960 and 2025. The standardised dataset of rocket launches has covered 16 geographical entities, including all the major spacefaring nations: US, Russia, China, India, Europe, and Japan. It includes over 330 different rocket configurations and 4,405 launches.According to the article, at the end of 2025, the cost of launching a satellite from India stood at $13,302 (Rs 12.7 lakh) per kg aboard rockets available in the country, an amount that was more than four times the figure of US, wherein the cost is $3,225 (Rs 3.1 lakh). The study finds the US to be the lowest among all the markets studied. As per the study, India is more expensive than the European Union, Russia, China and Japan.After India, Europe’s rocket launch cost is the next most expensive at $9,897 (Rs 9.5 lakh) per kg.However, a highly-placed source in the Dept of Space told TOI that the study has not factored in various concessions provided by Isro’s commercial wing NSIL. The Indian space agency gives “satellite customers 30% subsidy on cost of launches”. “Secondly, Indian customers save money in logistics and transport when launched from Sriharikota. Third foreign launchers normally send all satellites from one launcher to the same orbit, which leads to rise in launch cost as satellites piggyback on the primary payload have to be manoeuvred to their respective orbit,” the source said.Moreover, the Department of Space (DoS) and IN-SPACe has rolled out these financial incentives through two parallel frameworks: the Launch Services Price-support Scheme (LSPS) and Price Support Scheme. Both programmes are designed to significantly reduce the entry barriers for Indian non-govt entities. IN-SPACe also provides financial support ranging from 30% to 100% for satellite launches and related space infrastructure under its Rs 800 crore LSPS: up to 50% support for utilising Isro and Department of Space launch facilities; a 30% subsidy on launch costs (capped at $3,000/kg) for small vehicles carrying up to 500 kg; full 100% funding (capped at $13,000/kg for up to four missions) for payloads up to 120 kg.The Cambridge research also said, “The expense of launching cargo into space will plummet over the next few years, with the cost of reaching orbit forecast to more than halve between now and the end of the decade, and fall around 93% by 2040. The cost of sending a kilogram of payload into low Earth orbit, an average of $3,868 last year, is set to fall more than 58% to just $1,569 by 2030, and could reach as little as 273 US dollars per kilo by 2040, the study suggests.
Article Summary: India’s space price tag comes under scrutiny as cambridge research flags high launch costs, while the government says key subsidies and savings were overlooked. At the end of 2025, the cost of launching a satellite from india stood at $13,302 (rs 12.7 lakh) per kg.

Article Title: SIM card rules 2026: What changes from August 24 and how many connections can you have
Article Text:
Govt has directed the telecos to strictly enforce the rule of not issuing a new connection to any subscriber already having nine SIMs (representative image)

How the new SIM verification system will work

How many mobile connections can you have?

Most of India: Maximum 9 mobile connections

Jammu and Kashmir: Maximum 6

Assam: Maximum 6

North-East: Maximum 6

When will the new system become fully real-time?

The government has directed telecom service providers to stop individuals from obtaining mobile connections beyond the prescribed limit of nine, with a new system coming into effect from August 24.Under the Department of Telecommunications (DoT) instructions, telecom companies will have to identify subscribers who seek a new mobile connection after already reaching the maximum number allowed in their name and inform them that another connection cannot be provided.The move will initially operate on a post-facto basis, allowing telecom operators to carry out the verification one day after a connection is enrolled.However, the government has asked operators to shift to a real-time system for identifying and preventing excess connections by November 30.From August 24, telecom operators will have to take technical and organisational measures to identify subscribers attempting to obtain connections beyond the prescribed limit.The DoT circular said: “From 24.8.2026 onward, TSPs shall take appropriate technical and organisational measures to identify each subscriber who seeks to obtain mobile connections beyond the prescribed limit using the representative image of the photo of a subscriber....andcommunicate to him that he already has maximum number of mobile connections permitted to an individual and accordingly, a new mobile connection cannot be provided to him. ”To help operators carry out these checks, the DoT will make available on the Digital Intelligence Platform (DIP) from August 23 a representative image of the photograph of every subscriber who has already reached the prescribed limit.Telecom companies will have to download these images daily and use them to identify subscribers attempting to obtain additional mobile connections.Until the system is fully implemented on a post-facto basis, any connection activated beyond the permitted limit during a day will have to be immediately suspended until the issue is resolved.Under existing DoT instructions issued on August 9, 2012, an individual can hold a maximum of nine mobile connections in their name across all telecom operators and licensed service areas in India.However, a lower limit applies in certain regions:Customers are also required to provide a declaration in the Customer Application Form (CAF) stating the mobile connections already held in their name across telecom operators and licensed service areas.The government has set August 24 as the date from which telecom operators must begin identifying subscribers trying to obtain connections beyond the permitted limit.The initial system can operate on a post-facto basis, but telecom operators have been directed to integrate the checks into the enrolment and activation process in real time by November 30.The respective Licensed Service Areas (LSAs) will be the competent authorities to decide issues arising from implementation of the instructions.The DoT has directed telecom operators to decline new connections to subscribers who already have the maximum number of permitted SIM cards.
Article Summary: Govt has directed the telecos to strictly enforce the rule of not issuing a new connection to any subscriber already having nine sims. The move will initially operate on a post-facto basis, allowing telecom operators to carry out the verification one day after a connection is enrolled.

Article Title: 'Made-in-India chips power key space missions': IT minister Ashwini Vaishnaw
Article Text:
IT minister Vaishnaw posted on National Space Day.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Made-in-India semiconductor chips are powering key Indian space missions, supporting applications ranging from lunar and solar exploration to satellites and launch vehicles, Union electronics and IT minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said on Sunday.“Made in India chips are powering Indian Space Missions,” Vaishnaw said in a post on X on National Space Day.According to the ministry of electronics and information technology (MeitY), semiconductor components designed and manufactured domestically are being used across India's space programme, strengthening the country's push for technological self-reliance.A key contributor to this capability is the Semiconductor Laboratory (SCL) in Mohali, which develops and manufactures flight-grade semiconductor components designed to withstand the extreme conditions of space.SCL produces specialised components, including radiation-hardened chips, electro-optical CCD and CMOS imagers, application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs), and sensors used to measure parameters such as pressure, acceleration, temperature and acoustics.These indigenous components have already been deployed in major Indian space missions, according to news agency ANI. The Chandrayaan-3 lunar lander carried an Indian-made camera chip developed by SCL Mohali for its imaging systems during the mission to the lunar surface.India's solar mission, Aditya-L1, uses radiation-hardened analogue-to-digital converter (ADC) chips manufactured by SCL for scientific observations of the Sun.Indigenous semiconductor technology is also being used in launch vehicles. SCL's Vikram processor is deployed in satellites and rockets, providing onboard computing capabilities required during missions.The ministry said the growing ability to design and manufacture critical space-grade semiconductor components domestically is strengthening technological independence across India's space ecosystem.With India planning more space missions, locally manufactured chips are expected to play an increasingly important role in supporting the country's scientific, satellite and launch infrastructure.
Article Summary: It minister vaishnaw posted on national space day. Semiconductor laboratory (scl) in mohali develops and manufactures flight-grade semiconductor components. Chandrayaan-3 lunar lander carried an indian-made camera chip.

Article Title: Medical device makers flag new sterilisation labelling rule
Article Text:
The industry had sought an exemption through the Medical Device Technical Advisory Group (MDTAG) (representative image)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Medical device manufacturers have raised concerns over a new government rule requiring companies to print the licence number of an outsourced sterilisation facility on device labels, saying it could add to compliance burden and delay exports.The health ministry, in a notification dated August 14, 2026, amended the Medical Devices Rules, 2017, requiring manufacturers that outsource sterilisation to a licensed facility to mention its licence number on the device label. The requirement will become mandatory six months after the notification.The Association of Indian Medical Device Industry (AiMeD) has opposed the move, saying manufacturers are already being asked to obtain “loan licences” for using external gamma radiation or ethylene oxide (EO) sterilisation facilities.AiMeD said manufacturers had sought an exemption through the Medical Device Technical Advisory Group (MDTAG), but the new labelling requirement has instead added another compliance burden.The association said the rule could affect export shipments, as manufacturers may not be able to switch to another sterilisation facility if the one named on the packaging has a backlog or is unavailable. It claimed this could delay shipments by two to three weeks, compared with about a week earlier.AiMeD also questioned the need to print the subcontractor's details on the product, saying manufacturers remain responsible for quality and traceability, with batch-level records already allowing the sterilisation process to be tracked.The industry body has sought clarity on whether overseas manufacturers and their sterilisation facilities will also need Indian licences and whether the requirement will apply to their packaging.It has also sought clarity on how manufacturers should handle existing packaging stock before the new requirement takes effect.The notification provides a six-month transition period and was issued after the government considered objections and suggestions received on the draft rules and consulted the Drugs Technical Advisory Board.AiMeD has urged the government to reconsider the requirement, saying patient safety and traceability should be ensured without affecting the competitiveness of Indian manufacturers and their exports.
Article Summary: The health ministry has amended the medical devices rules, 2017. It requires manufacturers that outsource sterilisation to a licensed facility to mention its licence number on the device label. The association of indian medical device industry (aimed) has opposed the move.

Article Title: Soon, no need for physical boarding cards at immigration
Article Text:
From Sept 1, flyers can use e-boarding passes at India’s immigration counters; physical passes won’t be stamped

NEW DELHI: Starting Sept 1, people flying in and out of India will no longer be required to provide a physical boarding card at the immigration counter. Travellers can show their e-boarding cards instead. This major change by Bureau of Immigration could pave the way for more seamless international travel once e-passports become more common.Senior FRRO (Delhi) Deepak Yadav's communication says after immigration cleara-nce, the boarding pass is stamped by the immigration officer. "It has, however, been observed that this process causes inconvenience to passengers, and instances of errors in reading boarding passes due to improper or incorrect stamping, have also been reported," he said.The new measure will come into effect from Sept 1. "Physical boarding passes will continue to be accepted at the Immigration counters, however, these will not be stamped," Yadav's circular adds.Junior Union minister for external affairs KV Singh told Parliament this month, "The authentication of e-chip passport and its integration with IVFRT (immigration, visa, foreigners' registration and tracking) application for utilisation across immigration posts at international airports in India is under process."

Article Title: Who is Gautam Rangarajan? Indian-origin strategist appointed to key role by UK PM Andy Burnham
Article Text:
Indian-origin strategist Gautam Rangarajan.

Who is Gautam Rangarajan ?

What will Gautam Rangarajan do at No. 10?

Burnham's government overhaul

British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has appointed Indian-origin strategist and former BBC executive Gautam Rangarajan as an Expert Adviser on Structure and Process in a newly created role at 10 Downing Street.Rangarajan, who brings decades of experience in strategy, organisational transformation and media, is set to take up the position this week.Rangarajan is a senior strategist and media executive with more than two decades of experience across media, creative industries and public service broadcasting.Before his new government role, he spent more than 30 years at the BBC, beginning his career as a radio music producer and eventually rising to become the broadcaster's Group Director for Strategy and Performance.His experience includes developing strategy in rapidly changing markets, leading large-scale transformation initiatives and handling complex policy and financial negotiations.The exact details of Rangarajan's responsibilities are yet to be outlined. However, the UK PM's office said his appointment draws on his experience in corporate strategy and transformation.His role comes as Burnham undertakes a broader restructuring of the machinery of government, including the creation of the Office for the Prime Minister and Cabinet.Rangarajan is expected to play a role in the planned transformation at the heart of the British government.Away from strategy and public service, Rangarajan also has a creative side. He describes himself as a professional choral singer and music producer, alongside his work in corporate strategy and organisational transformation.The appointment comes as Burnham reshapes his government following his recent rise to the role of Labour Party leader and Prime Minister.His administration has announced structural changes, including the launch of No. 10 North in Manchester and the creation of the Office for the Prime Minister and Cabinet.While the full scope of Rangarajan's new role remains unclear, his appointment places the former BBC executive at the centre of the UK government's planned transformation.
Article Summary: Indian-origin strategist gautam rangarajan appointed as expert adviser on structure and process at 10 downing street. He brings decades of experience in strategy, organisational transformation and media. The appointment comes as andy burnham reshapes his government following his recent rise to the role of labour party leader and pm.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Michael J. Fox: "I think the scariest person in the world is the person with…" - a lesson on humour, perspective and facing hard times with lightness
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Michael J. Fox (AP photo)

Quote of the day by Michael J. Fox

"I think the scariest person in the world is the person with no sense of humor"

Where this quote actually comes from

Why humour matters most during genuinely difficult stretches

How humour actually helps people manage stress

Why laughing at your own mistakes actually matters

Why humour can genuinely strengthen relationships

Michael J. Fox's own perspective on adversity

Why humour is not the same thing as avoiding a real problem

Why being naturally serious is not actually a flaw

Other memorable quotes by Michael J. Fox

"One's dignity may be assaulted, vandalized and cruelly mocked, but it can never be taken away unless it is surrendered."

"I am careful not to confuse excellence with perfection."

"Family is not an important thing. It's everything."

"Acceptance doesn't mean resignation; it means understanding that something is what it is and that there's got to be a way through it."

Why people still find meaning in this quote

Humour can genuinely change how a difficult moment actually feels. A stressful situation seems lighter once someone finds a reason to laugh, and a serious problem often becomes easier to approach once it can be seen from another angle. It can create a little distance from fear, frustration and uncertainty, even when the circumstances themselves have not changed. Michael J. Fox , the actor and Parkinson's disease advocate, put a striking twist on that idea. "I think the scariest person in the world is the person with no sense of humor," he said. Not being able to laugh, in his framing, is not simply a personality quirk. It genuinely limits how someone can respond to life, and coming from someone who has lived with a serious, lifelong illness for decades, the line carries a good deal more weight than a passing joke.This line comes from an interview Fox gave to journalist Amy Wallace, published on Reader's Digest's website. Fox is not really suggesting that a humourless person is dangerous in any literal sense. He is pointing at the seriousness that tends to surround someone who cannot laugh at themselves, cannot recognise irony, and cannot find any lightness in a genuinely difficult moment. Humour creates real distance from a problem.It lets someone acknowledge that something is hard without letting it completely take over.Life inevitably brings disappointment, uncertainty and real stress. Humour cannot solve every problem on its own, but it can genuinely change how someone responds to one. Being able to laugh during a hard period offers a small emotional break, and it can help people communicate when a direct, serious conversation feels too uncomfortable to actually have. None of this means every situation deserves to be treated as a joke. Humour and genuine seriousness can exist side by side.Stress tends to narrow someone's attention down entirely onto the immediate problem in front of them. A moment of real laughter can interrupt that cycle. Research into humour and stress has suggested that positive humour can genuinely influence mood and help people cope with stressful experiences, and laughter itself is linked to physiological changes, including a release of muscle tension. None of this should be overstated. Humour is never a substitute for professional help or a practical solution when someone faces a genuinely serious problem. As an everyday coping tool, though, it can offer a genuinely useful shift in perspective.One of the most valuable forms of humour is simply being able to laugh at your own missteps. Nobody gets everything right. People mispronounce words, misjudge situations and occasionally embarrass themselves, and someone who can acknowledge a mistake without being consumed by embarrassment tends to find it easier to actually learn from it. Self-directed humour also tends to make social interactions considerably more comfortable, since it signals that a person does not expect flawless perfection from either themselves or anyone else around them.Shared laughter helps people form real connections. Friends, colleagues and family members often use humour to build a sense of familiarity and trust, and a well-placed joke can break tension that a serious conversation might struggle to shift on its own. There is an important line here worth being clear about, between humour that actually brings people together and humour that humiliates someone else. Jokes built on cruelty or prejudice tend to damage relationships rather than genuinely strengthen them, and the most constructive kind of humour has never really needed anyone else to get hurt.Fox became one of the most recognisable actors of his generation through films and television, including Back to the Future and Family Ties. In 1991, at the age of 29, he was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease. He later made the diagnosis public and became a prominent advocate for Parkinson's research through the Michael J. Fox Foundation. His public approach to living with the condition has consistently included honesty, genuine optimism and humour, which gives his comments about laughter an extra dimension. His point was never that difficult experiences are inherently funny. It is that holding onto a sense of humour can help someone preserve real perspective while actually facing a genuine challenge. His decades-long relationship with humour, cultivated alongside a chronic illness he never chose, reveals that laughter was never a denial of hardship for Fox, but a deliberate, hard-won tool for maintaining perspective and genuine hope through real adversity.There is a meaningful difference between using humour to cope with something difficult and using it to avoid actually dealing with it at all. Some problems genuinely require serious attention and real action, and nobody can simply laugh away financial difficulty, illness or grief. What humour can offer instead is a small amount of emotional breathing space while someone continues addressing the actual underlying issue, which is really the whole distinction worth holding onto here.Fox's quote is deliberately provocative, and it should not be read as suggesting that serious people are inherently unpleasant. Some people naturally have quieter personalities, or simply express humour in a different way. The broader lesson is really about flexibility rather than personality type. Someone who can be genuinely serious when it matters, while still finding moments of humour elsewhere, tends to have more ways of responding to life's challenges than someone who treats every single situation with exactly the same level of weight.Humour is easy to underrate, since it can look insignificant next to more obviously serious qualities like intelligence or discipline. Even so, the ability to laugh genuinely shapes how people communicate, handle their own mistakes and respond to real difficulty. Fox's quote offers a deliberately provocative reminder that life does not always need to be approached with complete seriousness. There will be moments when humour is genuinely inappropriate, and problems that cannot be laughed away at all. In between those moments, though, holding onto a sense of humour tends to keep people connected, flexible and hopeful, which is really the whole point behind the line.
Article Summary: "i think the scariest person in the world is the person with no sense of humor" michael j. Fox, actor and parkinson's disease advocate. Not being able to laugh is not simply a personality quirk. It genuinely limits how someone can respond to life. Michael j. Fox was one of the most recognisable actors of his generation.

Article Title: Micron CEO Sanjay Mehrotra's 'reminder' to everyone investing in AI and calling it 'big': Right now, there is no AI without ...
Article Text:
Micron CEO feels AI is creating a more durable source

Demand outstripping supply

US chipmaker Micron reaches $1 trillion market capitalization

Micron CEO Sanjay Mehrotra recently said that artificial intelligence has fundamentally transformed the memory industry, long known for its boom-and-dust cycles. “Today there is no AI without memory. AI systems need more memory. They need higher performance memory. They need lower power memory,” Mehrotra told CNBC’s Jim Cramer on Mad Money. “So, the value of memory, that equation has totally changed.” His remarks came as Micron builds a vast semiconductor fabrication site near its Boise, Idaho headquarters, part of a planned $250 billion investment in U.S. manufacturing and research. The Boise complex will eventually house two fabs, each the size of 10 football fields, with the first expected to begin wafer production in mid‑2027.Mehrotra, who co‑founded SanDisk and has worked in chips for over 40 years, said AI is creating a more durable source of demand across data centers, autonomous vehicles, robots, and consumer devices. “Memory today is essential. That’s why I call it the strategic infrastructure of the AI era,” he said.Micron still cannot produce enough to meet demand. Mehrotra said data‑center customers want about 50% more supply than Micron can commit.The company has signed five‑year strategic agreements with 16 customers, with more added since its June earnings call, giving it greater visibility into long‑term demand. “All our customers across our end markets will buy everything that we make,” he said.In related news, recently, US chipmaker Micron Technology briefly crossed a market value of $1 trillion on May 26 as investor excitement around AI continued to drive demand for memory chips. According to a report by news agency Reuters, the sharp rally made Micron one of the biggest winners of the AI boom, with its shares rising more than 17% during trading. Micron’s stock jumped after brokerage UBS raised its price target on the company to $1,625 from $535, the report said. The company’s shares rose as much as 19.3% during the session before easing slightly later.As cited in the Reuters report, analysts say the surge reflects growing demand for advanced memory chips used in AI data centers and cloud infrastructure. The company’s rise also highlights how investors are now focusing beyond graphics chipmakers and looking at firms supplying key AI hardware components. “The need for pure memory has increased rapidly over very short periods of time, and clearly, Micron sits at the center of it,” Art Hogan, chief market strategist at B. Riley Wealth, told Reuters. “Today's crossing of the $1 trillion mark for Micron is just an exclamation point on the story of the massive amount of demand needed to run data centers in this AI revolution,” he added.
Article Summary: Micron ceo feels ai is creating a more durable source of demand across data centers, autonomous vehicles, robots, and consumer devices. Us chipmaker micron technology briefly crossed a market value of $1 trillion on may 26 as investor excitement around ai continued to drive demand for memory chips.

Article Title: Microsoft is hiring a legal engineer to teach lawyers across the company how to…
Article Text:
Microsoft wants a lawyer who can build AI agents, and it is paying up to $278,900 for one

Why Microsoft wants a lawyer who can also write software

The legal engineer job is spreading from startups to Big Tech

Microsoft has spent the past two years telling everyone else that AI is about to change how work gets done. Now it wants someone to prove the point inside its own legal department. The company has posted a job for a principal legal engineer, an unusual hybrid role that asks for a practising attorney who can also ship software, with base pay topping out at $278,900 a year.The listing, spotted on LinkedIn this week by Business Insider, puts the hire inside Microsoft's Customer & Partner Solutions group, the arm that supports the company's commercial business. The work is deliberately hands-on: building AI agents, sharpening prompts, and training attorneys and paralegals to actually use the tools. "This is a role for a builder," Microsoft wrote in the job description, adding that the person will partner directly with engineering rather than advise from the sidelines. Microsoft did not respond to Business Insider's request for comment.Lawyers were the corporate world's great tech holdouts for decades, understandably nervous about tools that could get one detail wrong in a 90-page agreement. That resistance is thinning. Clients are now pushing outside firms toward tools like Harvey and Claude for Legal to turn work around faster and bill less for it.The same pressure has moved in-house. Legal teams are betting that software can handle contract edits and policy drafting, letting them keep more of the early work and hand outside counsel matters that are already halfway done.Microsoft has a head start here because it builds some of these tools itself. Its lawyers already use Copilot for routine work, including contract review, where it compares a draft against similar agreements, flags issues and suggests edits that match company policy. Harvey is being rolled out across Corporate, External, and Legal Affairs.Until recently, legal engineer was mostly a startup title, filled by ex-lawyers with technical chops who sat close to customers. Palantir posted its own embedded legal engineer role last month, promising to turn manual workflows into automated ones.Microsoft wants a law degree and at least seven years of practice. Experience with Harvey or Copilot is preferred. Base pay starts at $147,000.
Article Summary: Microsoft wants a lawyer who can build ai agents, and it is paying up to $278,900 for one. The company has posted a job for a principal legal engineer, an unusual hybrid role that asks for a practising attorney who can also ship software. The work is deliberately hands-on: building ai agents and training attorneys and paralegals to use the tools.

Article Text:
Beats 360 to get a new design

Beats 360 may be offered in six colours

Beats 360 price and features

Apple’s unreleased Beats 360 over-ear headphones have allegedly appeared on several retail websites, revealing details about their design, colours, features and pricing ahead of an official launch. Listings for the headphones were spotted on Amazon U.K. and other retail websites before being removed. The leak suggests that the Beats 360 will have a new design compared with the current Beats Studio Pro and Solo 4. The headphones are expected to offer active noise cancellation, all-day battery life, IPX4 water and sweat resistance and support for both Apple and Android devices. Retail listings have also revealed a $299 US price.The leaked images show the Beats 360 with a different design from the company's existing over-ear headphones. The headphones feature a separate padded section underneath the headband, while the earcups have a more open mesh design.The padded section can reportedly be removed, as can the ear cushions. Retail listings also mention an Extra Cushion Kit, with Performance Knit and UltraPlush options. The leaked headphones also appear to be the same model that football player Lamine Yamal was seen wearing in Instagram posts earlier this summer.The Beats 360 is expected to launch in Sky, Black, Navy, Cloud, Pink and Volt. The six colour options would give the headphones a wider range of finishes than the current Beats Studio Pro and Solo 4.The Volt version has a bright neon-yellow finish.Retail listings have also revealed pricing. One listing showed the headphones at $299, while another listed them at £331.99. The Beats 360 is expected to feature active noise cancellation, with one product description claiming up to 1.75 times more noise cancellation than the Beats Studio Pro.The headphones reportedly do not use Apple's H2 chip or another Apple chip. They will, however, work with both Apple and Android devices. The headphones were also listed with an IPX4 rating for water and sweat resistance.The leaked product information claims the Beats 360 can offer all-day battery life even with ANC turned on. The headphones are said to fold flat and are expected to come with a woven ripstop fabric carrying case.

Article Title: IBM CEO Arvind Krishna on his letter that ‘shocked’ business world, sent company's stock over 25 percent down, making it 'worst day' in IBM history
Article Text:
IBM CEO Arvind Krishna

Why IBM CEO thinks it was important to ‘tell’ beforehand

Facing an impending quarterly earnings miss driven by shifting enterprise IT budgets and rising AI distractions, IBM Chairman and CEO Arvind Krishna opted for radical transparency -- a move that triggered a historic stock plunge but is reported to have aligned with his core leadership philosophy. In an interview with CRN, IBM CEO Krishna detailed the high-stakes decision to pre-announce the 115-year-old tech giant's financial shortfall eight days before its scheduled July 22 earnings call. The disclosure sent IBM shares tumbling more than 25%, marking one of the steepest single-day declines in the company's history.IBM's underperformance stemmed from enterprise clients pausing infrastructure projects to front-load spending on data center hardware amid supply constraints and surging costs. Additionally, Krishna noted that customer attention had been diverted by security debates surrounding an AI model released by Anthropic. He reduced IBM's expected full-year revenue growth for the year by more than $600 million, saying that the fall is in part due to some clients pushing out IBM infrastructure projects to pay for the growing cost of supply constrained memory, storage, servers and other data center infrastructure.Rather than holding the bad news for the standard earnings cycle, Krishna fell back on a long-standing operating principle: "If there’s a hard thing to be done, do it earlier rather than later," Krishna told CRN.By clearing the bad news early, Krishna aimed to pivot the official earnings call away from post-mortem explanations and toward strategic fixes. "Time will tell whether that was the right decision. I tend to think it was," Krishna said. "Otherwise, we would have been spending the last week explaining the hesitation as opposed to what we are going to do to go fix it."The decision highlights the pressures facing IBM as it balances heavy investments in generative AI and long-term quantum computing against Wall Street's short-term expectations. When asked by CRN about potential vulnerability to activist investors or board friction following the market reaction, the CEO, who took the helm in April 2020, remained pragmatic about corporate oversight."If you falter, one should always be just prepared is my view," Krishna said, adding that public CEOs must constantly evaluate whether they are delivering sufficient returns. "And activists, at the end, if I look at the good side, are trying to come in to say, 'I need better returns for clients and for investors.' And if that’s the goal, then one should be prepared to deal with them. That is just the nature of today’s world that we live in. "Krishna maintained that his primary strategy to protect the company's innovation roadmap remains centered on client satisfaction and workforce investment.IBM CEO Krishna reasoned the Q2 weakness to deal ‘deferral, and not destruction’. He said, “This was deferral and not destruction.” Krishna made the statement while talking to analysts during IBM’s latest quarterly earnings call with analysts. Krishna’s confidence comes in part from the fact that one-third of those largest infrastructure projects requiring a lot of customer CapEx have already closed.
Article Summary: Ibm chairman and ceo arvind krishna opted for radical transparency. The disclosure sent ibm shares tumbling more than 25%, marking one of the steepest single-day declines in the company's history. Krishna: "if there’s a hard thing to be done, do it earlier rather than later"

Article Title: A Chinese robot ‘dies’ after hitting safety wall during World Humanoid Robot Games running test
Article Text:
Chinese robot hits safety wall during running test

World Humanoid Robot Games set for 2026

Unitree unveils robot that is claimed to run faster than Usain Bolt

A bipedal Chinese humanoid robot allegedly training for World Humanoid Robot Games has gone viral after it lost control during a running test. In a viral video shared by X (formerly Twitter) user @pianhangx, the robot can be seen running toward the barrier before crashing into it, with its body bending sharply at the waist and sparks coming from the machine. The dramatic crash has led to social media users describing the incident as the moment the “robot dies.” The incident took place as robots prepare for the 2026 edition of the World Humanoid Robot Games in Beijing, China. The event kickstarts on August 22 and will showcase a record 2,056 robots and 666 teams this year.According to reports, the humanoid robot was taking part in a training session for the running competition when it appeared to lose control. In the video, it can be seen running at high speed and failing to stop before hitting the safety wall. The impact caused the robot's body to bend at the waist, while sparks could be seen coming from it.The video was shared on social media on August 20 and quickly attracted attention. At the time of writing, it has garnered over 13 million views. “The robot ran too fast to brake in time, crashed into the cushion, and broke its waist,” the Twitter user wrote.Times of India was not able to independently verify the viral video.The World Humanoid Robot Games first took place in Beijing in 2025. The event brings humanoid robots together for competitions based on sports and other activities. As mentioned above, the 2026 event is expected to be significantly larger, with 666 teams and more than 2,056 robots taking part across 50 events.The competition will include running and other sports, while robots will also take part in activities such as dance performances and serve as flag bearers.In another news, Chinese robotics firm Unitree has unveiled a new "Superman" humanoid robot that is claimed to outrun and outjump top human athletes. The company said the robot can reach a top speed of 12.66 meters per second (m/s) — faster than the roughly 12.4 m/s top speed achieved by Usain Bolt during his world-record 100m run in 2009.
Article Summary: Chinese robot hits safety wall during running test. Incident took place as robots prepare for the 2026 edition of the world humanoid robot games in beijing, china. The video was shared on social media on august 20 and quickly attracted attention. At the time of writing, it has garnered over 13 million views.

Article Title: Elon Musk’s Starlink seeks fresh India approval; says it will help ‘least served’...
Article Text:
What Elon Musk said about Starlink’s India launch

Starlink’s second attempt after an earlier rejection

Direct‑to‑device tech imminent

Regulatory and security challenges

Elon Musk’s Starlink has renewed efforts to launch satellite communication services in India. According to a report by Economic Times, the company is resubmitting an application to the Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre (IN‑SPACe) for approval of its Gen 2 constellation. The new system would operate at altitudes of 340–615 km in low earth orbit and introduce direct‑to‑device (D2D) connectivity, a feature Musk has touted as critical for reaching underserved communities.Elon Musk underscored the importance of Starlink’s India push in a recent post on X, saying the service would help the “least served” communities. Replying to a post on X, Musk wrote, ‘Starlink would help the least served in India, especially in rural areas.’The Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre (IN-SPACe) had rejected an earlier application from the Elon Musk-owned company for its planned 30,000-satellite internet constellation a few years ago, citing non-conformity in certain features and spectrum bands. According to a person familiar with the details, who spoke on condition of anonymity since the specifics aren't public, the company has now applied for authorisation of its Gen 2 constellation, which would operate at an altitude of 340-615 km in low earth orbit.Starlink, operated by SpaceX and the world's largest LEO satellite operator, remains bullish on India's satcom market, which industry watchers describe as still nascent but carrying significant long-term potential. The company had originally applied for both Gen 1 and Gen 2 constellations to begin services in India, but IN-SPACe approved only the Gen 1 constellation, comprising 4,408 LEO satellites offering traditional broadband services, in July 2025.India is considering opening more spectrum bands for satellite communications and allowing D2D features, prompting Starlink’s reapplication. If approved, the Gen 2 constellation could give Starlink a significant edge by enabling mobile connectivity directly to consumer devices, bypassing traditional telecom networks.So far, no non‑geostationary satellite operator — including Starlink, OneWeb, or Jio’s SES joint venture — has launched commercial services in India due to pending security clearances and spectrum allocation. The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has issued pricing recommendations, but the government has yet to finalize rules. Telecom operators have warned that D2D services could threaten their business and have pushed for satellite firms to face the same regulatory obligations.
Article Summary: Starlink has renewed efforts to launch satellite communication services in india. The company is resubmitting an application to the indian national space promotion and authorisation centre (in‑space) for approval of its gen 2 constellation. The new system would operate at altitudes of 340–615 km in low earth orbit and introduce direct‑to‑device (d2d) connectivity.
